MapleStory: Idle RPG × Oracle

How Nexon Uses Oracle

The insights Oracle delivered across the pilot — each on-screen finding shown with the real frame it came from.

31 Aug – 8 Sept 2026: 7 Nexon analysts · 25 sessions · 89 questions · Warehouse = Snowflake SQL (full population) · Video = BlueStacks recordings (observed sample) · Both = cross-source.
36.8%
of shop-active players made a real cash payment (July)
61.3%
of installs are Organic + Google Ads; ~1 in 6 unmatched
75%+
of sessions end in idle / sleep — not a rage-quit
6 : 1
checkout abandons are user-cancels vs. technical errors
Section 01

One workflow, run from every angle: who pays, who doesn't, and why

  1. Orient — confirm which Snowflake tables exist and how terms are defined (first-purchase = cash only, NEW/RETURN rules, pLTV tiers).
  2. Size a cohort in the warehouse — e.g. "8,119 first-payers in Aug week 1", "830 high-pLTV non-payers", "81,166 churn-risk".
  3. Bridge to BlueStacks video — how many of that cohort have a recording, then watch what they actually did on screen.
  4. Pull the clip — the exact moment: a purchase, a wall, an error, an idle exit.
The examples below are drawn from real analyst sessions. Oracle answered from live data and declined to profile any named individual.
Section 02

Monetization & first purchase

The paying funnel, and what the very first purchase looks like — with the on-screen moment.

On screen: "블루 다이아 구매하기 150,000 / KRW 150000" purchase popup; top-bar Blue Diamond 45 → 150,045 after.
45 → 150,045
A real-money top-up, caught on screen

A player charges KRW 150,000 for 150,000 Blue Diamonds — the balance jumps from 45 to 150,045 — specifically to afford a Companion Summon pack. The wallet opens to clear a wall, not for cosmetics.

Video dykim1890 · Blue-Diamond first-spend study
36.8%
Shop-active → cash payer

Of 380,666 shop-active players in July, 36.79% made a real cash payment.

Warehouse dykim1890 · 09-04
On screen: Blue Diamond shop tab: x1,500 (₩1,500), x3,000, x9,000 … up to x150,000.
31.5%
One cheap SKU is the front door

A single 1,500 KRW pack (HotDealProduct_102) is the first purchase for 31.5% of first-payers. The Blue-Diamond shop shows the ladder from ₩1,500 to ₩150,000.

Both dykim1890 · 09-08
On screen: "T1 Weapon Hot Deal" — EUR 1.19, components diamond x1,500 + T1 weapon x1 (Ellinia).
₩/€/kr
Hot-deal offers are the paid entry point

First real-money purchases are overwhelmingly direct packs (81%) over currency top-ups (19%). Hot-deal offers recur across regions — a T1 Weapon deal at €1.19, a Raid deal at $10.9, a 4th-Job deal at SEK 79.

Video dykim1890 / whiterod
On screen: Shop 會員 (Membership) tab — "楓谷特殊會員券 (30天)" Maple Special Membership, TWD 65.
browse, no buy
Membership browsed, then closed

The 'look then leave' pattern on screen: a player opens the shop at the end of a session, lands on the Membership tab, and closes without buying.

Video dykim1890 · browse-then-close reps
4.29M/day
Shop volume & spiky revenue

~4.29M shop events/day in July (133.1M total), weekend-heavy. Revenue concentrates hard: Aug 13 alone was 24.2% of the period's cash-shop revenue.

Warehouse dykim1890 · 09-04/07
Section 03

Churn & retention

Who leaves, and what the warehouse cannot see about them.

On screen: "어빌리티 변환 핫딜" (Ability Conversion Hot Deal) popup — "9,000 부족" (insufficient), KRW 9,000 — dismissed.
ad instead of pay
High-value non-payers dismiss the offer

830 top-25%-pLTV new users who haven't paid reach the shop, see a price they lack the currency for, and dismiss it — then lean on rewarded ads. Recoverable revenue with the right offer.

Both dykim1890 · 09-07
On screen: Shop offering a free "500 佩里多特" (500 Blue Mushrooms) via 觀看廣告 (Watch Ad).
ad = daily loop
At-risk players farm ads, not spend

An at-risk player (Day-1, $0 spent) opens the shop only to claim an ad-gated reward. Rewarded ads are the free pipeline that substitutes for paying.

Video dykim1890 · at-risk study
On screen: "離線獎勵" (Offline Reward) 06:32 / 24h — Lv.98, gold 131,848 (Magatia Lab).
idle exit
The last session before going quiet

A churning player's final session: log in, claim 6.5 hours of offline rewards, pop a buff, auto-combat — then drift. The exit is calm, not a rage-quit.

Video dykim1890 · 3 last-session study
81,166
Churn-risk pool the video barely sees

The warehouse flags 81,166 still-active but at-risk players; only 25 have a recording. A huge at-risk pool is almost invisible on screen — a coverage gap.

Both dykim1890 · 09-07
Section 04

Player behavior & UX (from the screen)

What players hit around the shop, in combat, and where they stall.

On screen: "Notice: The session has expired." over the [Ad] Red Diamond x1000 / Watch Ad popup (Normal Shop).
session expired
An ad-reward that fails mid-claim

A player tries to watch an ad for 1,000 Red Diamonds in the shop — and the claim dies on a "session has expired" error. The free pipeline itself is leaky.

Video dykim1890 · ad-watch study
On screen: "CHAPTER 17 STAGE 07" fail screen — 離開 (Leave) / 重新開始 (Restart), auto-close 4s.
fail → quit
The wall that ends a session

Combat-failure exits are the distinct #2 way sessions end (11.2%). On screen: a stage fails, the Leave/Restart screen appears, and the player leaves.

Video dykim1890 · fail-then-quit reps
75%+
Sessions end quietly, not in rage

Over three-quarters of sessions end in idle/sleep; combat failure is a distant second (11.2%). Retention has to reach players between sessions, not mid-session.

Warehouse dykim1890 · 09-07
On screen: "28. Herb Town", "Stage 9/10", "Stage 10 Challenge" — clearly legible.
read on screen
Video reads exact stage & price text

Oracle reads on-screen text directly — stage/chapter numbers, prices, item counts — the layer the warehouse has none of. Here: the exact stage a player is on.

Video dykim1890 · stage-number study
Section 05

Payment failures & technical health

What breaks at checkout and in-session.

7.1% · 6:1
Most checkout drop-off is choice, not bugs

Of 38.3M market-checkout attempts (Jul 1 – Aug 15), 7.1% didn't complete — and user cancels outnumber technical errors ~6:1. But the error slice is real and recoverable.

Warehouse whiterod · 09-08
On screen: "Daily Mission Boost Star Force Hot Deal", NOK 275 — "Waiting for server response." overlay + spinner.
server hang
A real purchase, stuck on the server

A willing buyer taps a Star Force Hot Deal (NOK 275) — and the purchase hangs on "Waiting for server response." This is the recoverable slice inside the abandonment number.

Video whiterod · payment-failure study
On screen: "Waiting for server response." freeze over gameplay (Leafre Dragon Nest).
6–8%
Crashes ~0, but sessions still stall

Across 4 builds crash rate is near zero, yet 6–8% of sessions hit a technical issue — "Session Expired" the most common and disruptive. On screen: an in-overworld freeze.

Both whiterod · 09-08
On screen: Title "TAP TO START" + "Waiting for server response." (also "Loading table..").
stuck at start
New players stalled before they begin

Server-connection stalls hit the title/loading screen too — a player sits on "TAP TO START" behind a "Waiting for server response" overlay. First impression, blocked.
